key_insight: MeanFlowNFT adapts forward-process RL to MeanFlow by converting average-velocity sampling into an induced instantaneous-velocity objective, enabling reward optimization without sacrificing few-step generation speed.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical way to align fast generative models with human or task-specific rewards while retaining the low-latency sampling advantages needed in production systems.
method: Construct an induced instantaneous-velocity predictor from the MeanFlow identity.
Apply the DiffusionNFT forward-process RL objective to this predictor.
Keep inference on average velocity so sampling stays few-step and efficient.
evidence_signal: Experiments on image and video generation show consistent improvements, including outperforming prior RL-tuned few-step generators on most metrics and reaching 84.33 VBench on Wan 2.1 with 4 steps versus 82.57 for a 50-step RL baseline.
watch_item: The approach depends on a correct average-to-instantaneous velocity bridge, so implementation errors or distribution shift could weaken the policy-improvement guarantee in practice.
paper_title: MeanFlowNFT: Bringing Forward-Process RL to Average-Velocity Generators
